literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期重点文献按发表日期、相关性、证据等级和研究质量综合排序，研究结果与综述证据分别核验后形成以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 完成调查问卷的 224 名与会者中有 65 例(5 例确诊,60 例疑似)。流行病学调查发现,食用新鲜水果(比值比 [OR]:5.3;95% 置信区间 [95% CI]:2.4-12.6;p < 0.001)和腌肉(OR:2.7;95% CI:1.2-6.2;p = 0.02)与疾病显着相关。 [10.33321/cdi.2026.50.042]
已鉴定出 35 种与脊椎动物相关的病毒,其中包括 9 种潜在的新物种和 3 种具有人畜共患潜力的病毒(首尔正汉坦病毒和人类冠状病毒 OC43)。在啮齿类动物中发现了两种此前未报告的病毒(刺猬首尔正汉坦病毒和犬星状病毒),揭示了跨目传播风险。武汉和深圳表现出不同的流行模式,气象变量独立解释了5.0%的病毒群落组成变化。 [10.1038/s42003-026-10711-0]
分区模型虽然与平均模拟结果一致,但未能可靠地预测任何单一爆发事件。 [10.3390/appliedmath6070115]
提供的证据没有明确说明直接观察到的主要结果。 [10.64898/2026.07.18.739367]

news.headline_zh: 2026年7月阿拉斯加游轮诺如病毒疫情频发,CDC监测显示废水病毒载量升高。
news.lead_zh: 2026年7月,美国阿拉斯加水域多艘游轮接连报告诺如病毒爆发,涉及乘客与船员共计145人。CDC监测数据显示,诺如病毒活动水平处于高位且呈上升趋势,公共卫生机构正加强对此类聚集性事件的监测与应对。
key_findings_zh: 林德布拉德探险队运营的“国家地理海鸟”号在阿拉斯加水域于7月10日至15日航程中报告了第三次胃肠道疾病爆发,62名乘客中有18人出现症状,前两次爆发已确认为诺如病毒。
公主邮轮公司的“红宝石公主”号在6月12日至7月2日的阿拉斯加与加拿大航程中爆发诺如病毒,导致102名乘客和23名船员患病,这是该公司2026年的第三起诺如病毒事件。
CDC监测数据显示,美国诺如病毒活动水平目前处于“高”位且呈上升趋势,新流行毒株GII.17[P17]可能加剧了这一趋势,尽管详细监测数据仍在完善中。
CDC已记录2026年游轮上7起达到公开通报阈值的胃肠道疫情,凸显了对船上疾病聚集性事件的严格审查,同时FDA已将多州环孢子虫病爆发追溯到单一墨西哥供应商。
游轮运营商普遍采取了加强清洁消毒、隔离患病人员、收集样本检测以及咨询CDC船舶卫生计划等措施,以遏制疫情进一步扩散。
尽管采取了干预措施,CDC仍将监督重点描述为远程监控而非现场调查,且部分爆发原因尚未完全确定,存在一定的不确定性。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 当前阿拉斯加游轮航线面临较高的诺如病毒传播风险,新流行毒株GII.17[P17]的活跃以及废水监测显示的高病毒载量表明疫情可能持续。游轮运营商已实施严格的卫生干预措施,但CDC强调需持续加强监测与报告机制,以应对潜在的快速传播风险。
news.caveats_zh: 部分爆发原因尚未完全确定,CDC的监督主要依赖远程监控而非现场调查,且详细的流行病学监测数据仍在完善中。此外,部分报道来源的翻译状态为英文回退,可能影响信息的完整性。
news.headline_en: Frequent Norovirus Outbreaks on Alaska Cruises in July 2026, CDC Monitoring Shows Elevated Wastewater Levels.
news.lead_en: In July 2026, multiple cruise ships in Alaskan waters reported successive norovirus outbreaks affecting a total of 145 passengers and crew. CDC monitoring data indicate norovirus activity levels are high and rising, prompting public health authorities to strengthen surveillance and response.
key_findings_en: Lindblad Expeditions' National Geographic Sea Bird reported a third gastrointestinal outbreak during its July 10–15 Alaska voyage, with 18 of 62 passengers symptomatic; prior outbreaks were confirmed as norovirus.

Princess Cruises' Ruby Princess experienced a norovirus outbreak during its June 12–July 2 Alaska and Canada voyage, sickening 102 passengers and 23 crew, marking the line's third norovirus incident in 2026.

CDC monitoring shows norovirus activity in the U.S. is currently 'high' and trending upward, potentially driven by a newly circulating strain (GII.17[P17]), though detailed surveillance data are pending.

CDC has logged seven gastrointestinal outbreaks on cruise ships in 2026 that met its public-notification threshold, highlighting heightened scrutiny of onboard illness clusters, while FDA traced a multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak to a single Mexican supplier.
Cruise operators implemented enhanced sanitation, isolated sick individuals, collected samples for testing, and consulted the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program to curb further spread.
Despite interventions, CDC describes oversight as remote monitoring rather than active on-site investigation, and the cause of some outbreaks remains undetermined, indicating ongoing uncertainty.
news.trend_or_risk_en: The current risk of norovirus transmission on Alaskan cruise routes is elevated, with the active circulation of the new strain GII.17[P17] and high wastewater viral loads suggesting sustained activity. Cruise operators have implemented strict hygiene interventions, but CDC emphasizes the need for continued monitoring and reporting to manage the risk of rapid spread.
news.caveats_en: The cause of some outbreaks remains undetermined, and CDC oversight relies primarily on remote monitoring rather than on-site investigation. Additionally, detailed epidemiological surveillance data are still being refined, and some reports have English-only translations, potentially affecting information completeness.
news.brief_en: In July 2026, multiple cruise ships in Alaskan waters reported successive norovirus outbreaks, affecting 145 passengers and crew. CDC monitoring indicates norovirus activity is high and rising, potentially driven by a new strain GII.17[P17]. Cruise operators implemented enhanced sanitation and isolation measures, while CDC logged seven gastrointestinal outbreaks on ships in 2026. The agency emphasizes remote monitoring and ongoing investigation into undetermined causes.

papers.title: Investigation of a norovirus outbreak at a catered social event, Australian Capital Territory, 2024.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: An outbreak of gastrointestinal illness was notified, affecting attendees at a private function in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) in 2024. Investigations were conducted to determine the infectious agent, source of illness and mode of transmission, as well as to determine any public health actions required to prevent further illness. METHODS: Function attendees were surveyed using a modified standard gastroenteritis questionnaire. A confirmed outbreak case was defined as an individual who was unwell after attending the event and had a norovirus-positive clinical sample; a probable outbreak case was defined as an individual who was unwell with clinically compatible symptoms after attending the event. A case-control study was conducted to identify food items associated with illness. Food safety inspections were performed, and food samples were tested at the ACT Government Analytical Laboratory. Clinical samples were collected from unwell attendees and from an asymptomatic food handler. RESULTS: There were approximately 250-500 attendees at the function; 224 attendees completed the questionnaire and there were 65 cases (5 confirmed and 60 probable). A food handler who had previously been unwell, and who prepared fruit and meat platters for the function more than 96 hours after their symptoms had resolved, subsequently tested positive for norovirus. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2024 年,澳大利亚首都直辖区 (ACT) 爆发了胃肠道疾病,影响了参加私人活动的与会者。我们进行了调查以确定传染源、疾病来源和传播方式,并确定预防进一步疾病所需的公共卫生行动。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们进行了一项病例对照研究,以确定与疾病相关的食品,参加活动的大约有 250-500 名参加者,其中 224 人完成了调查问卷,65 人被确定为病例。
elements_zh.methods: 使用修改后的标准胃肠炎调查问卷对活动参加者进行了调查,并从身体不适的参加者和无症状的食品处理人员中收集了临床样本。进行了食品安全检查,并在首都领地政府分析实验室对食品样本进行了测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 完成调查问卷的 224 名与会者中有 65 例(5 例确诊,60 例疑似)。流行病学调查发现,食用新鲜水果(比值比 [OR]:5.3;95% 置信区间 [95% CI]:2.4-12.6;p < 0.001)和腌肉(OR:2.7;95% CI:1.2-6.2;p = 0.02)与疾病显着相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 流行病学和临床证据表明,尽管场所具有良好的食品处理和洗手习惯,诺如病毒还是通过受污染的新鲜水果和腌肉拼盘传播。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,需要继续在食品准备环境中进行有效的手部卫生教育,特别是在胃肠道疾病之后,以降低诺如病毒传播的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有发现公众面临任何持续风险,但由于依赖自我报告的数据和调查的回顾性,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:据悉爆发了胃肠道疾病,影响了 2024 年澳大利亚首都领地 (ACT) 私人活动的参加者。进行了调查以确定传染源、疾病来源和传播方式,并确定预防进一步疾病所需的任何公共卫生行动。方法:使用修改后的标准胃肠炎调查问卷对活动参加者进行调查。确诊的疫情病例被定义为参加活动后身体不适且临床样本呈诺如病毒阳性的个人;可能的暴发病例被定义为参加活动后出现不适并出现临床症状的个人。进行了一项病例对照研究,以确定与疾病相关的食品。进行了食品安全检查,并在首都领地政府分析实验室对食品样本进行了测试。临床样本是从身体不适的参加者和无症状的食品处理人员那里收集的。结果:大约有 250-500 名与会者参加了此次活动;224 名与会者填写了调查问卷,共有 65 例病例(5 例确诊病例,60 例疑似病例)。一名之前身体不适的食品处理人员在症状消失超过 96 小时后准备了水果和肉类拼盘,随后诺如病毒检测呈阳性。环境健康调查显示,该场所有良好的饮食习惯和洗手习惯;调查发现公众没有持续面临的风险。食品样本检测未发现任何细菌性食源性病原体。流行病学调查发现,食用新鲜水果(比值比 [OR]:5.3;95% 置信区间 [95% CI]:2.4-12.6;p < 0.001)和腌肉(OR:2.7;95% CI:1.2-6.2;p = 0.02)与疾病显着相关。结论:流行病学和临床证据表明诺如病毒是通过受污染的新鲜水果和腌肉拼盘传播的。尽管该场地有良好的食品处理和洗手习惯,但这很可能是由于一名食品处理人员在活动前一周身体不适,并在症状消失超过 96 小时后才准备了相关食品。这次疫情调查表明,安全食品实践和排除期可以减少但不能完全消除风险。我们的研究结果强调了在食品准备环境中继续进行有效手部卫生教育的必要性,特别是在胃肠道疾病之后。

analysis_zh.main_results: 完成调查问卷的 224 名与会者中有 65 例(5 例确诊,60 例疑似)。流行病学调查发现,食用新鲜水果(比值比 [OR]:5.3;95% 置信区间 [95% CI]:2.4-12.6;p < 0.001)和腌肉(OR:2.7;95% CI:1.2-6.2;p = 0.02)与疾病显着相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 流行病学和临床证据表明,尽管场所具有良好的食品处理和洗手习惯,诺如病毒还是通过受污染的新鲜水果和腌肉拼盘传播。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,需要继续在食品准备环境中进行有效的手部卫生教育,特别是在胃肠道疾病之后,以降低诺如病毒传播的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有发现公众面临任何持续风险,但由于依赖自我报告的数据和调查的回顾性,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Introduction Noroviruses is a major cause of outbreaks and sporadic acute gastroenteritis (AGE) across all age groups. Although the GII.4 norovirus has been the primary cause of most AGE outbreaks, Non-GII.4 norovirus has been reported globally. Aim We aimed to report an increase in GII.17 norovirus outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in multiple provinces of China during the second half of 2024. Methods Data and specimens from AGE outbreaks (January 2022–December 2024) were collected. Samples were tested via real-time RT-PCR; positive GII.17[P17] samples underwent sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Results Among 1,579 norovirus outbreaks, 1,225 were genotyped. The first halves of 2022–2024 saw co-circulation of genotypes GII.3[P12], GII.4 Sydney, GII.17[P17], and GII.7[P7]. GII.4 Sydney dominated the second halves of 2022 (46.15%) and 2023 (51.63%). Strikingly, in the second half of 2024, GII.17[P17] became predominant, causing 75.28% of outbreaks. This shift was driven by a novel GII.17 variant (Romania-2021 like, subcluster C2), first detected in February 2024, which replaced the previous Kawasaki 308-like variant. The novel variant predominantly affected the 6–18 years age group (54.97%) and elementary schools (34.33%). Relative to Cluster D, this novel variant harbors five amino acid mutations in antigenic epitopes, one mutation in the histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding site, and two deletions. Conclusions A novel GII.17 variant has overtaken GII.4 as the predominant norovirus strain in China since late 2024, underscoring the need for continued molecular surveillance. papers.title: Metatranscriptomics reveals urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has advanced our understanding of wildlife-associated viruses and enabled identification of potential zoonotic pathogens. However, most studies remain geographically limited, with few systematic comparisons of virome compositions across urbanization gradients. To address this gap, we conducted large-scale sampling in two densely populated Chinese megacities-Wuhan and Shenzhen-with distinct climates. We collected 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans, enabling comparative analysis of urban rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents. We identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses. Among them, 9 were potentially novel species, including Norovirus and Orthopicobirnavirus species, and 3 had zoonotic potential, namely Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43 (HCoV_OC43). We also discovered two viruses previously unreported in rodents, Erinaceus hedgehog Seoul orthohantavirus and Canine astrovirus, which revealed cross-order transmission risk. Additionally, 22 high-risk viruses were identified, with Wuhan and Shenzhen showing distinct prevalence patterns. Our analysis shows that inter-city rectal virome divergence is structured by meteorological variables, independently explaining 5.0% of the variation in viral community composition. Our findings highlight the importance of spatial distance in shaping the distribution and transmission of rodent-borne viruses. These insights are essential for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments.

source_records.title: Metatranscriptomics reveals urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.
source_records.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has advanced our understanding of wildlife-associated viruses and enabled identification of potential zoonotic pathogens. However, most studies remain geographically limited, with few systematic comparisons of virome compositions across urbanization gradients. To address this gap, we conducted large-scale sampling in two densely populated Chinese megacities-Wuhan and Shenzhen-with distinct climates. We collected 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans, enabling comparative analysis of urban rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents. We identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses. Among them, 9 were potentially novel species, including Norovirus and Orthopicobirnavirus species, and 3 had zoonotic potential, namely Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43 (HCoV_OC43). We also discovered two viruses previously unreported in rodents, Erinaceus hedgehog Seoul orthohantavirus and Canine astrovirus, which revealed cross-order transmission risk. Additionally, 22 high-risk viruses were identified, with Wuhan and Shenzhen showing distinct prevalence patterns. Our analysis shows that inter-city rectal virome divergence is structured by meteorological variables, independently explaining 5.0% of the variation in viral community composition. Our findings highlight the importance of spatial distance in shaping the distribution and transmission of rodent-borne viruses. These insights are essential for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Urbanization is expanding globally, yet systematic comparisons of rodent viromes across urbanization gradients remain scarce, leaving gaps in understanding zoonotic risk dynamics in megacities. The study aimed to address this by investigating how urbanization and environmental factors shape rodent virome composition and zoonotic potential in densely populated Chinese cities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed large-scale sampling in two Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, with distinct climates, collecting 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans. The design enabled comparative analysis of urban rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents across these urbanization gradients.
analysis.methods: Rodent rectal samples were subjected to metagenomic sequencing to identify vertebrate-associated viruses and assess zoonotic potential. Meteorological variables were recorded and analyzed to determine their contribution to viral community composition variation.
analysis.main_results: Thirty-five vertebrate-associated viruses were identified, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43). Two viruses previously unreported in rodents were discovered (Erinaceus hedgehog Seoul orthohantavirus and Canine astrovirus), revealing cross-order transmission risk. Wuhan and Shenzhen exhibited distinct prevalence patterns, and meteorological variables independently explained 5.0% of viral community composition variation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that urbanization gradients and meteorological factors structure rodent virome divergence, highlighting previously underappreciated spatial and environmental drivers of zoonotic risk. Novelty lies in the systematic cross-city comparison and identification of cross-order transmission risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides actionable insights for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments by identifying high-risk viruses and environmental correlates of viral diversity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two megacities and rectal sampling, which may not capture full zoonotic risk across all rodent tissues or broader geographic areas. Despite this, the large sample size and systematic cross-city design strengthen the evidence base.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how urbanization and environmental factors shape rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in two Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, by collecting and sequencing rectal samples from 1,072 rodents across four species. Using metagenomic sequencing, the authors identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43). Two viruses previously unreported in rodents were discovered, revealing cross-order transmission risk. Urban and meteorological variables independently explained 5.0% of viral community composition variation, with distinct prevalence patterns observed between cities. The findings highlight the importance of spatial and environmental drivers in structuring rodent virome divergence and zoonotic risk, providing actionable insights for surveillance and mitigation in high-density urban environments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 城市化正在全球范围内扩张,但对跨城市化梯度的啮齿动物病毒组的系统比较仍然很少,这使得人们在了解大城市的人畜共患病风险动态方面存在差距。该研究旨在通过调查城市化和环境因素如何影响人口稠密的中国城市中的啮齿动物病毒组组成和人畜共患潜力来解决这一问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在气候不同的中国两个特大城市武汉和深圳进行了大规模采样,收集了来自四个经常与人类互动的物种的 1,072 只啮齿动物。该设计能够对城市直肠病毒动态和跨这些城市化梯度的啮齿动物的人畜共患风险进行比较分析。
elements_zh.methods: 对啮齿动物直肠样本进行宏基因组测序,以鉴定脊椎动物相关病毒并评估人畜共患病的可能性。记录并分析气象变量以确定它们对病毒群落组成变化的贡献。
elements_zh.main_results: 已鉴定出 35 种与脊椎动物相关的病毒,其中包括 9 种潜在的新物种和 3 种具有人畜共患潜力的病毒(首尔正汉坦病毒和人类冠状病毒 OC43)。在啮齿类动物中发现了两种此前未报告的病毒(刺猬首尔正汉坦病毒和犬星状病毒),揭示了跨目传播风险。武汉和深圳表现出不同的流行模式,气象变量独立解释了5.0%的病毒群落组成变化。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,城市化梯度和气象因素构成了啮齿动物病毒组的差异,突显了先前未被充分认识的人畜共患病风险的空间和环境驱动因素。新颖之处在于系统性的跨城市比较和跨订单传播风险识别。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究通过识别高风险病毒和病毒多样性的环境相关性,为主动监测和缓解高密度城市环境中新出现的人畜共患威胁提供了可行的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注两个大城市和直肠采样,可能无法捕获所有啮齿动物组织或更广泛地理区域的完整人畜共患病风险。尽管如此,大样本量和系统的跨城市设计加强了证据基础。

papers.abstract_zh: 宏基因组测序增进了我们对野生动物相关病毒的理解,并能够识别潜在的人畜共患病原体。然而,大多数研究仍然局限于地理范围,很少对不同城市化梯度的病毒组组成进行系统比较。为了解决这一差距,我们在两个人口稠密、气候不同的大城市——武汉和深圳进行了大规模采样。我们收集了来自四个经常与人类互动的物种的 1,072 只啮齿动物,从而能够对啮齿动物的城市直肠病毒动态和人畜共患病风险进行比较分析。我们鉴定出 35 种与脊椎动物相关的病毒。其中,9个潜在新种,包括诺如病毒和正双核病毒属,3个具有人畜共患潜力,即汉城正汉坦病毒和人类冠状病毒OC43(HCoV_OC43)。我们还在啮齿动物中发现了两种以前未报告的病毒,即刺猬首尔正汉坦病毒和犬星状病毒,这揭示了跨目传播的风险。此外,还发现了 22 种高风险病毒,其中武汉和深圳表现出不同的流行模式。我们的分析表明,城市间直肠病毒组差异是由气象变量构成的,独立解释了病毒群落组成变异的 5.0%。我们的研究结果强调了空间距离在影响啮齿动物传播病毒的分布和传播方面的重要性。这些见解对于主动监测和缓解高密度城市环境中新出现的人畜共患威胁至关重要。

papers.title: Editorial: Advances in optical methods for biological sample characterization
papers.abstract: Optical methods have quietly become one of the most productive points of contact between physics and biology. The proper use of laser-tissue interactions can reveal the orientation of a single collagen fibril, the redox state of a mitochondrion, or the vibrational fingerprint of a virus, often without staining, fixing, or otherwise disturbing the sample under study. The four contributions gathered in this Research Topic, Advances in Optical Methods for Biological Sample Characterization, sample that breadth directly: a mechanistic study of second harmonic generation in the cornea, a critical review of the trade-offs built into fluorescent labelling, a forward-looking perspective on the field as a whole, and a plasmonic biosensing platform built to tell two closely related viruses apart. Read together, they show how mature certain optical techniques have become, and how much interpretive and instrumental work still remains.We opened this Research Topic with a deliberately wide scope, inviting work on bioimaging, biosensors, optical tweezers, particle tracking, and AI-assisted data analysis. In our own Perspective (Avila et al.), we used these five domains as a scaffold for a broader argument: that the next substantial gains in optical biological characterization are likely to come less from any single modality reaching a new performance ceiling, and more from combining modalities, from tighter integration with computation, and from a sharper distinction between what an optical signal shows and what it is generally assumed to mean. The three remaining contributions to this Research Topic each speak to that argument from a different angle.Boutkhil et al. take on a problem that has limited the clinical translation of second harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy for some time: backward-detected SHG signal, the only geometry realistically available for in vivo imaging, has historically been harder to interpret than the cleaner forward signal obtained from thin, ex vivo sections. Imaging intact porcine corneas in a custom pressure-controlled chamber, the authors show that the periodic high-and low-intensity bands long read in backward images as discrete "collagen bundles" are in fact an artifact of collagen crimp, the natural waviness of corneal lamellae. Raise the intraocular pressure and the fibres straighten; the bands fade in step. The authors are candid that a complete quantitative model linking the forward-to-backward signal ratio to tissue structure remains out of reach, but the structural mechanism they identify should change how the next generation of corneal SHG images, and the diagnostic claims built on them, are read.A second axis of the same general problem, quite literally whether to label a sample at all, runs through the review by Cuevas-Galindo and Jiménez-Sánchez. Small-molecule fluorescent probes are indispensable tools, but the authors build a sustained case that the same properties that make a probe bright and selective, high-affinity binding, lipophilic partitioning, excitedstate reactivity, also make it an active participant in the biology it is meant to report on. Their discussion of calcium indicators, whose buffering capacity measurably reshapes the signalling kinetics they are used to track, gives a concrete anchor to an argument that can otherwise stay abstract. The review does not call for abandoning labels; it positions label-free approaches, autofluorescence imaging of NAD(P)H and flavins, fluorescence lifetime imaging, as a benchmark against which any probe's effect on the underlying physiology should be checked, and it surveys middle-ground strategies, including HaloTag and SNAP-tag constructs, bioorthogonal fluorogenic chemistry, and ratiometric sensing, that try to narrow that gap.The fourth contribution moves from imaging to sensing. describe a plasmonic metasurface, patterned with Y-shaped nanocavity arrays and tuned to 785 nm excitation, that supports surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) sensitive enough to discriminate human from murine norovirus particles by their vibrational signature alone. analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the intersection of optical methods and biological sample characterization, focusing on bioimaging, biosensors, optical tweezers, particle tracking, and AI-assisted data analysis to assess how these techniques reveal biological structures and functions without sample disturbance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The editorial presents a Research Topic comprising four contributions analyzed through a scaffold of five optical domains, emphasizing the integration of modalities, computation, and signal interpretation rather than single-modality advances.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Optical techniques like second harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) can reveal structural and biochemical details, but their interpretation is often confounded by artifacts, probe-induced perturbations, or signal geometry, necessitating careful validation and statistical analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Backward-detected SHG signals are misinterpreted as discrete collagen bundles due to collagen crimp artifacts, and fluorescent probes can alter the biological processes they aim to measure, highlighting unresolved challenges in signal fidelity and probe neutrality.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future work should prioritize developing quantitative models linking signal geometry to tissue structure, validating label-free approaches against probe-based methods, and advancing statistical tools for distinguishing closely related biological targets in diagnostics.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial synthesizes advances in optical methods for biological characterization, highlighting their ability to probe biological structures and functions without sample disturbance. It critiques the interpretive challenges of techniques like SHG microscopy and fluorescent labeling, where artifacts and probe-induced perturbations complicate signal fidelity. The review underscores the need for integrating modalities, computation, and statistical analysis to improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly in distinguishing closely related pathogens. Key gaps include incomplete quantitative models for signal interpretation and the disruptive effects of probes on biological systems, which future research must address to enhance clinical and research applications.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了光学方法和生物样品表征的交叉点,重点关注生物成像、生物传感器、光镊、粒子跟踪和人工智能辅助数据分析,以评估这些技术如何在不干扰样品的情况下揭示生物结构和功能。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该社论提出了一个研究主题,包括通过五个光学领域的支架分析的四项贡献,强调模态、计算和信号解释的集成,而不是单一模态的进步。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 二次谐波发生 (SHG) 显微镜和表面增强拉曼光谱 (SERS) 等光学技术可以揭示结构和生化细节,但它们的解释常常受到伪影、探针引起的扰动或信号几何形状的干扰,需要仔细验证和统计分析。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于胶原卷曲伪影,向后检测的 SHG 信号被误解为离散的胶原束,而荧光探针可以改变它们想要测量的生物过程,突出显示信号保真度和探针中性方面尚未解决的挑战。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的工作应优先开发将信号几何与组织结构联系起来的定量模型,根据基于探针的方法验证无标记方法,以及改进用于区分诊断中密切相关的生物靶标的统计工具。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了光学方法和生物样品表征的交叉点,重点关注生物成像、生物传感器、光镊、粒子跟踪和人工智能辅助数据分析,以评估这些技术如何在不干扰样品的情况下揭示生物结构和功能。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该社论提出了一个研究主题,包括通过五个光学领域的支架分析的四项贡献,强调模态、计算和信号解释的集成,而不是单一模态的进步。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 二次谐波发生 (SHG) 显微镜和表面增强拉曼光谱 (SERS) 等光学技术可以揭示结构和生化细节,但它们的解释常常受到伪影、探针引起的扰动或信号几何形状的干扰,需要仔细验证和统计分析。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于胶原卷曲伪影,向后检测的 SHG 信号被误解为离散的胶原束,而荧光探针可以改变它们想要测量的生物过程,突出显示信号保真度和探针中性方面尚未解决的挑战。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的工作应优先开发将信号几何与组织结构联系起来的定量模型,根据基于探针的方法验证无标记方法,以及改进用于区分诊断中密切相关的生物靶标的统计工具。

papers.title: Establishing wastewater metagenomics as a quantitative pathogen monitoring tool with normalization
papers.abstract: Abstract Wastewater metagenomic sequencing (WW-MGS) enables simultaneous detection of hundreds of pathogens, but its use for quantitative pathogen tracking has not been robustly validated. Like wastewater PCR (WW-PCR), WW-MGS is affected by biases from variable fecal dilution and sample processing, but must additionally contend with the compositional structure of sequencing data, where a taxon’s apparent abundance depends on the abundance of every other taxon in the sample. Simple summaries such as a pathogen’s fraction of total reads may therefore be poorly suited to quantitative use. We retrospectively evaluated seven normalization approaches that attempt to control for these sources of bias against a baseline of total read relative abundance, using 1,425 samples from the CASPER consortium spanning 25 U.S. Each approach was compared against WW-PCR and clinical data across eight total pathogens. Among the normalization strategies we evaluated, tobamovirus markers, diet-derived plant viruses abundant in human stool, performed best. Normalizing WW-MGS data by tobamovirus-genus counts improved median site concordance for 18 of 19 pathogen and comparison-source combinations. Gains were largest for year-round-circulating SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus and smaller for sharply seasonal pathogens such as influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, where baseline concordance was already high. Tobamovirus normalization rarely degraded concordance, with median gains roughly five times larger than median losses. Tobamovirus-normalized WW-MGS reached clinical concordance comparable to targeted WW-PCR, supporting its use as a quantitative trend-monitoring tool alongside pathogen-agnostic detection.

papers.title_zh: 建立废水宏基因组作为标准化的定量病原体监测工具
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Wastewater metagenomic sequencing (WW-MGS) enables simultaneous detection of hundreds of pathogens, but its use for quantitative pathogen tracking has not been robustly validated. Like wastewater PCR (WW-PCR), WW-MGS is affected by biases from variable fecal dilution and sample processing, but must additionally contend with the compositional structure of sequencing data, where a taxon’s apparent abundance depends on the abundance of every other taxon in the sample. Simple summaries such as a pathogen’s fraction of total reads may therefore be poorly suited to quantitative use. We retrospectively evaluated seven normalization approaches that attempt to control for these sources of bias against a baseline of total read relative abundance, using 1,425 samples from the CASPER consortium spanning 25 U.S. Each approach was compared against WW-PCR and clinical data across eight total pathogens. Among the normalization strategies we evaluated, tobamovirus markers, diet-derived plant viruses abundant in human stool, performed best. Normalizing WW-MGS data by tobamovirus-genus counts improved median site concordance for 18 of 19 pathogen and comparison-source combinations. Gains were largest for year-round-circulating SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus and smaller for sharply seasonal pathogens such as influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, where baseline concordance was already high. Tobamovirus normalization rarely degraded concordance, with median gains roughly five times larger than median losses. Tobamovirus-normalized WW-MGS reached clinical concordance comparable to targeted WW-PCR, supporting its use as a quantitative trend-monitoring tool alongside pathogen-agnostic detection.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要废水宏基因组测序(WW-MGS)可以同时检测数百种病原体,但其在定量病原体追踪中的应用尚未得到充分验证。与废水 PCR (WW-PCR) 一样,WW-MGS 受到可变粪便稀释和样品处理偏差的影响,但还必须应对测序数据的组成结构,其中一个分类单元的表观丰度取决于样本中所有其他分类单元的丰度。因此,简单的总结(例如病原体占总读数的比例)可能不太适合定量使用。我们回顾性评估了七种标准化方法,这些方法试图根据总读数相对丰度的基线来控制这些偏差来源,使用来自 CASPER 联盟跨越 25 个美国的 1,425 个样本。每种方法都与八种病原体的 WW-PCR 和临床数据进行比较。在我们评估的标准化策略中,烟草花病毒标记物(人类粪便中富含的饮食来源的植物病毒)表现最好。通过烟草花叶病毒属计数标准化 WW-MGS 数据提高了 19 种病原体和比较源组合中 18 种的中位点一致性。全年传播的 SARS-CoV-2 和诺如病毒的增益最大,流感和呼吸道合胞病毒等季节性病原体的增益较小,这些病原体的基线一致性已经很高。烟草病毒标准化很少会降低一致性,中值增益大约是中值损失的五倍。烟草花病毒归一化的 WW-MGS 达到了与靶向 WW-PCR 相当的临床一致性,支持其用作定量趋势监测工具以及病原体不可知检测。

papers.title: Environmental prevalence of enteric viruses across the covid-19 pandemic: A three-year monitoring study.
papers.abstract: Enteric viruses are continuously excreted in high concentrations in human feces and are disseminated into aquatic environments through treated and untreated wastewater, much of which is ultimately discharged into coastal marine waters. Environmental surveillance of these pathogens may therefore reflect their circulation in human populations and serve as an early-warning tool for the emergence of new viruses or variants, as well as increased transmission of existing ones. In this study, we investigated the occurrence and molecular diversity of major gastroenteric viruses - adenovirus, noroviruses, rotavirus - together with other enteric viruses with variable clinical relevance, in coastal marine waters of Campania Region (Southern Italy). Viral prevalence was evaluated according to season, sampling year, and type of wastewater discharge. A total of 500 marine water samples were collected, of which nearly half (44.0%) tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, presumably influenced by the epidemiological dynamics associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. Notably, phylogenetic analyses revealed that most environmental viral sequences were identical or closely related to strains previously identified in human clinical cases from the same geographical area, supporting a strong epidemiological link between human infections and environmental contamination. Overall, these findings underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for public health risk assessment within a One Health framework.

papers.title: Research on Mathematical Modeling of Infectious Disease Spread on Cruise Ships
papers.abstract: Cruise ships, characterized by high density, enclosed environments and shared facilities, have become amplifiers for infectious disease outbreaks; however, predicting transmission in such settings remains challenging due to small initial case numbers. In this study, a mathematical modeling framework—including compartmental, small-world (SW), and scale-free (SF) network models—was developed to analyze the dynamics of hantavirus and norovirus transmission on recent cruise ship outbreaks. The results show that when the initial number of exposed or infected individuals is extremely small (e.g., 1–2 persons), disease spread is dominated by stochasticity, causing substantial variation between individual simulations and mean model predictions. Notably, SF networks exhibited lower transmission risk under these conditions, contradicting the theoretical expectation that when the population is large, SF networks facilitate the spread of disease. The compartmental model, while consistent with average simulation outcomes, failed to reliably predict any single outbreak event. In conclusion, for closed environments such as cruise ships with very few initial cases, stochastic variability is essential, and single-outbreak outcomes should be understood as highly contingent rather than deterministically predictable.

papers.abstract_zh: 邮轮以其高密度、封闭环境、共用设施等特点,成为传染病爆发的放大器;然而,由于初始病例数较少,预测这种情况下的传播仍然具有挑战性。在这项研究中,开发了一个数学建模框架——包括隔室、小世界(SW)和无标度(SF)网络模型——来分析最近游轮爆发中汉坦病毒和诺如病毒传播的动态。结果表明,当初始暴露或感染个体数量极少(例如 1-2 人)时,疾病传播以随机性为主,导致个体模拟与平均模型预测之间存在巨大差异。值得注意的是,SF 网络在这些条件下表现出较低的传播风险,这与人口较多时 SF 网络促进疾病传播的理论预期相矛盾。分区模型虽然与平均模拟结果一致,但未能可靠地预测任何单一爆发事件。总之,对于初始病例很少的游轮等封闭环境,随机变异至关重要,单次疫情爆发的结果应被理解为高度偶然的结果,而不是确定性的可预测结果。

papers.title: Diagnostic and Microbiological Impact of Multiplex Syndromic Testing for Acute Infectious Gastroenteritis in a Regional Laboratory Network: A Real-World Before–After Study
papers.abstract: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (AIG) is caused by diverse bacterial and viral enteric pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, limiting conventional pathogen-directed workflows. This retrospective before–after study evaluated the diagnostic, microbiological, operational, and economic impact of multiplex molecular syndromic testing for AIG within a regional hub-and-spoke laboratory network in Italy. Two 19-month periods were compared: a pre-implementation period based on conventional diagnostics and a post-implementation period using multiplex syndromic panels as first-line tests. Diagnostic investigations totalled 25,574 before and 24,509 after implementation. Overall test positivity increased from 5.43% to 11.59% (p < 0.001), with significant increases for bacterial and viral targets. Pathogen detection events increased from 1388 to 2839, including broader detection of Campylobacter spp., Shigella spp./enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Yersinia enterocolitica, Aeromonas spp., Astrovirus, Sapovirus, and Norovirus genogroups. Mean turnaround time decreased from 63 to 47 h from sample collection and from 56 to 41 h from laboratory check-in. Although direct diagnostic costs increased moderately, total laboratory costs decreased when personnel costs were included, and cost per diagnostic detection declined from €233.80 to €120.86. Multiplex syndromic testing improved microbiological detection, diagnostic efficiency, turnaround time, and laboratory organisation in routine AIG diagnosis.

papers.title: Direct estimation of genotype fitness from time series
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous adapting populations, whether in laboratory evolution experiments or global-scale pandemics, experience complex evolutionary dynamics due to the interplay of selection, mutation, and stochasticity. Inference of individual genotypes' fitnesses therefore becomes difficult, especially when many lineages are competing and data are noisy. Existing fitness inference methods tend to rely on assumptions on the fitness landscape's maximum order of epistasis, or they require complicated iterative optimization algorithms to converge on fitness estimates. Here, we show that fitness landscapes can be computed from time series data, without any restrictions on epistatic order or iterative optimization, using a simple, closed-form mathematical expression that is easily implemented with standard matrix operations used commonly in linear algebra. We demonstrate successful fitness inference from noisy in silico evolutionary dynamics from four different noisy microscopic processes, including Wright-Fisher, Moran, ProSeD (serial dilution), and barcoded passage simulations. Then, we illustrate the broad applicability of the equation to five experimental time series datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution experiments, murine norovirus-1 serial passage experiments, and SARS-CoV-2 global genomic prevalence data. Our formula successfully infers fitnesses for even for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than top lineages, works with both laboratory evolution and epidemiological data, and can be implemented in most modern scientific programming languages.

Uh, it peaks, uh, during the summertime, uh, when people are eating more fruits and vegetables. And what happens is there's *** parasite in those items that gets into your body. It adheres to your gut, and matures, and then it causes *** very intense watery diarrhea. Most people resolve it on their own. Some can get awfully sick and need antibiotics to clear it. There are multiple different organisms that can cause *** diarrheal illness, norovirus, salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, and also Cyclospora. What makes Cyclospora different is that it causes an explosive diarrhea. The other organisms have different features. It could be fever, it could be bloody diarrhea, or other. But Cyclospora primarily is an explosive diarrhea. For most people, it lasts days, not weeks. For most people, they clear it on their own with just supportive care, meaning rest and hydration. But some individuals for whom it's persistent or intense need antibiotics to clear it. I would say that if your diarrhea is not intense, it's short duration and not associated with lightheadedness, fever, The inability to take in fluids, you're probably OK self-managing. If you have fever, persistent nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, are unable to keep up with your fluids. If you're very young, if you're old, if you have medical problems, and it's persisting, those are people that would benefit from an office evaluation. At the office, they're able to do testing such as we have right in our lab. And they take *** swab of the diarrhea, send it to our lab, and we can see if the organism is present. Common fruits and vegetables that cyclospore is found in include cilantro, basil, leafy greens, lettuce, salad mixes, spinach, uh, raspberries, blueberries. And what's *** feature of all of those items is they have rough irregular surfaces. So they're very difficult to fully clean. That's the biggest challenge. That's the biggest opportunity to reduce the risk of getting this infection. Well, people should not use things like bleach or other to clean surfaces. What they need to do is do other than just apply running water. They need some physical contacts against the food items themselves to clean the surfaces. So washing very well with clean water and then manually cleaning the fruit or vegetables generally will prevent the transmission. It's not clear if it's coming from farms. It's not clear if there are other sources involved. But again, the general approach of washing it vigorously with water and then manually cleaning the food items is the best strategy that we have. There's also not human to human transmission. The way this spreads is from *** person having diarrhea and some of that material getting into either food prep or food service. That's the way it can transmit. Um, in general, the, the therapy is to rest and keep up with your fluids. You wanna be very selective you're, you're using over the counter medication, medication that slows the diarrhea. You don't want to retain um the parasite in your system. That's the caution about using such medicines. Updated: 4:04 PM EDT Jul 17, 2026 Editorial Standards i Damali Ramirez Data Researcher/Curator The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and other state public health officials on Thursday linked an outbreak of cyclosporiasis to iceberg lettuce that Taylor Farms supplied to Taco Bell.Earlier this week, the CDC issued a multistate notice for cyclospora, a foodborne parasite that gets into people’s bodies, particularly their gut, and causes a diarrheal illness.The CDC is more likely to issue an outbreak notice when the level of public health concern is higher and the public threat is specific, according to its guidelines. The notice was the eighth the CDC issued this year so far, according to its data.More than 1,600 people reported getting sick after eating at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia. The FDA traced back a single supplier of the iceberg lettuce from Mexico used by these Taco Bell locations. Taco Bell is working to stop using this lettuce. The CDC is still investigating other outbreaks and illnesses of cyclosporiasis nationally that are unrelated to this outbreak. The Get the Facts Data Team analyzed data on CDC multistate foodborne outbreak notices issued since 2006 to determine which germs caused the most notices and which are commonly linked to illness, hospitalizations and deaths. How many multistate foodborne outbreak notices has the CDC issued since 2006?Since 2006, the CDC has issued 231 multistate foodborne outbreak notices, letting the public know what actions they can take to stay healthy. Salmonella was the foodborne germ with the most outbreak notices, at 116. Escherichia coli, also known as E. coli, had the second-most outbreak notices with 54, and Listeria had 38.How many cyclosporiasis outbreaks have there been previously? The Cyclospora surge is the first cyclosporiasis outbreak for which the CDC has issued a notice this year. The last time the health agency issued an outbreak notice for cyclosporiasis was in 2020 for a bagged salad mix. In total, there have been 10 outbreak notices for the parasite since 2006.What germs commonly cause foodborne illnesses? About 48 million people get sick from a foodborne illness each year, with about 128,000 ending up hospitalized and 3,000 deaths, according to the CDC. Norovirus is the leading foodborne germ that causes illness in the U.S. The highly contagious germ, sometimes called the "stomach flu" or "stomach bug," causes vomiting and diarrhea. Norovirus is also the leading cause of foodborne illness that results in hospitalization. But it’s Salmonella that leads in deaths in the U.S. and causes about 1.35 million infections every year. analysis.brief_en: A U.S. public-health explainer published on 17 July 2026 highlights Cyclospora, Salmonella, E. coli, and norovirus as leading causes of foodborne illness, noting that norovirus causes the most infections while Salmonella leads in deaths. The article also reports a current multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis linked to Taco Bell restaurants in five states, with more than 1,600 illnesses traced to iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms from Mexico. The U.S. CDC issued a multistate outbreak notice and the FDA identified the single supplier; Taco Bell is removing the implicated product. Cyclospora infection typically causes explosive watery diarrhea lasting days, with severe cases requiring antibiotics. The parasite spreads via contaminated produce with rough surfaces and cannot be transmitted person-to-person. Prevention focuses on vigorous washing and manual scrubbing of fruits and vegetables. The CDC continues investigating unrelated cyclosporiasis cases nationwide.

analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: More than 1,600 illnesses reported in the Taco Bell-linked outbreak; nationally, CDC issues 231 multistate foodborne outbreak notices since 2006 (Salmonella 116, E. coli 54, Listeria 38); cyclosporiasis outbreaks historically rare (10 notices since 2006, last in 2020); CDC estimates ~48 million foodborne illnesses, 128,000 hospitalizations, and 3,000 deaths annually in the U.S.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC issued a multistate notice for cyclosporiasis; FDA traced implicated lettuce to a single Mexican supplier; Taco Bell is discontinuing use; CDC continues investigating unrelated cyclosporiasis cases; guidance emphasizes washing produce with clean water and manual cleaning; no human-to-human transmission; testing via stool swab at clinical offices; source notes uncertainty about farm-level contamination origin.

news.title_zh: 沙门氏菌、大肠杆菌、诺如病毒是一些常见的食源性细菌 - WBAL-TV
news.source_body_en: A U.S. public-health explainer published on 17 July 2026 highlights Cyclospora, Salmonella, E. coli, and norovirus as leading causes of foodborne illness, noting that norovirus causes the most infections while Salmonella leads in deaths. The article also reports a current multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis linked to Taco Bell restaurants in five states, with more than 1,600 illnesses traced to iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms from Mexico. The U.S. CDC issued a multistate outbreak notice and the FDA identified the single supplier; Taco Bell is removing the implicated product. Cyclospora infection typically causes explosive watery diarrhea lasting days, with severe cases requiring antibiotics. The parasite spreads via contaminated produce with rough surfaces and cannot be transmitted person-to-person. Prevention focuses on vigorous washing and manual scrubbing of fruits and vegetables. The CDC continues investigating unrelated cyclosporiasis cases nationwide.

news.title: How Can You Avoid Norovirus 2026? - The People's Pharmacy
news.rss_summary_html: How Can You Avoid Norovirus 2026?  The People's Pharmacy
news.excerpt_original: How Can You Avoid Norovirus 2026? The People's Pharmacy
news.priority_tier_reason: 可信机构来源或已成功抓获正文
news.content: Norovirus is nasty! You do not want to catch this “stomach flu.” It is also called “winter vomiting disease” and “cruise ship virus.” This pathogen is incredibly contagious and is circulating far and wide. We know that people are fed up with viruses: coronaviruses, flu viruses, cold viruses, HMPV, etc. But norovirus 2025 is nasty! Public health authorities are reporting that cases are up substantially from previous years. They are beginning to suspect that a new strain is responsible for this stomach bug: GII.17[P17]. There are other strains out there, but this one has seemingly taken over. The most recent notice from the CDC is dated January 2, 2025, but there is not a lot of detailed information about what’s in store for us over the next several weeks. Given the latest trends, however, it looks like we are in for a literal S**T storm! Where Are People Suffering? Cruise ships are reporting an uptick in cases. And some early warning signs are flashing on land as well. I am especially fond of WastewaterScan’s dashboard. These are the folks who monitor sewage around the country. They have reported that SARS-CoV-2, RSV and influenza A are at high levels. They have also reported that norovirus is “high” and has been trending up over the last 3 weeks. Judging from their map, this intestinal virus is pretty well distributed around the United States. I fear that the CDC won’t have solid data for another week or so, but it would be prudent to be careful. More about that shortly. You will not easily forget a run-in with this intestinal apocalypse! Just contemplate the term “projectile vomiting.” Perhaps you have heard the expression “gut wrenching.” It is usually reserved for an emotionally challenging experience. I would like to suggest that you take that phrase literally. It should give you pause if you think norovirus is no big deal. What Are the Symptoms of Norovirus? Symptoms come on suddenly with severe vomiting and diarrhea. Victims may also have headaches, stomach cramps and fever. Reading about such symptoms doesn’t tell the real story, though. Here is what readers of our newsletter report: Mike gives you a sense of what this virus is like: “It does come on quickly, believe me! Hopefully you are near a bathroom when it strikes...like within a few steps! It is the only time in my life where I had to alternate sitting and kneeling for hours, outside of church. “I did not leave the bathroom for a few hours out of fear. Dehydration is very thorough and no doubt dangerous for many. If you first experience symptoms at home, cancel any plans for a few days because it will hunt you down. “This virus is almost impossible to avoid if you are caring for infected kids. It was 8 years ago and I still use it as a relative measure. “Well compared to noro....” You get the idea.” Pat also describes an intestinal “apocalypse”: “After Christmas dinner at our daughter’s house, EVERYONE that was there came down with norovirus! My husband hadn’t been feeling well (nausea) and went to bed early. “By 9:00 pm my nausea, stomach cramping, vomiting and diarrhea started with a cataclysmic explosion! If I’d known what was happening, I would have stayed on the toilet with a large bowl in my lap. I had no idea this would go on for 5 hours! Every time I had to vomit, the diarrhea would activate at the same time. “I would not wish this on my worst enemy, and I pray to God that I never get it again!” C. tells what happens when you are close to cruise ships: “I lived in the Caribbean with my office right on the harbor. One day I bought a salad from a fast food place where a lot of the cruise ship crew ate. The next day I thought I was going to die. I certainly wished I would because I was unbelievably miserable. “I literally could not even drink water the first day because it would trigger vomiting and dry heaves, coming out all ends. The second day I could suck on ice chips, and the third day I could take small sips of ginger ale. I was incredibly weak so I could barely stand up. It was the most excruciating stomach pain I’ve ever had in my life.” D. has another way to describe a norovirus attack: “I’m currently recovering from what is probably norovirus. I don’t know where I caught it but had been to the pharmacy, chiropractor and grocery store. Intestinal tsunami is a perfect description for the abdominal pain and the projectile vomiting.” K. demonstrates how contagious this bug can be: “Norovirus is as contagious as they say. I caught it and became very ill. I went to bed early because I didn’t feel well but had to get up because of the vomiting and extreme diarrhea. “On the way back from the bathroom, I passed out and woke up on the floor. I called the doctor in the morning. She advised hospitalization or Gatorade. My neighbor went to the store for me to get the Gatorade, but I didn’t realize how contagious norovirus is. She caught it from the money I gave her for the purchase!” As you can imagine, a condition that causes severe diarrhea and projectile vomiting could spread a lot of virus around. What’s more, it takes only a few viral particles to infect someone. How Do People “Catch” Norovirus? - “While sick, they shed billions of tiny viral particles in their stool and vomit. It takes a very small amount—as few as 18 viral particles—to make another person sick. People can get sick if they are exposed to a tiny amount of stool or vomit from an infected person. - They are most contagious when sick with vomiting and diarrhea, but may also infect others before symptoms start and after they feel better. - Because symptoms come on suddenly, an infected person who vomits in a public place may expose many people.” “Norovirus is hard to kill and stays on food, kitchen surfaces, and utensils. It can - Remain infectious on foods even at freezing temperatures and until heated above 140°F. - Stay on countertops and serving utensils for up to 2 weeks. - Resist many common disinfectants and hand sanitizers.” Can You Catch Norovirus From the Air? The CDC emphasizes that you can get norovirus by “touching surfaces or objects contaminated with norovirus and then putting your unwashed fingers in your mouth.” What the CDC does not mention is airborne transmission. The National Health Service (NHS) in the UK offers a somewhat different perspective, though. It does list contaminated food as one source of spread. The NHS also describes touching contaminated surfaces or objects. But here is the big difference between the US public health services and the NHS: “Norovirus spreads very easily in public places such as hospitals, nursing homes and schools. “You can catch it if small particles of vomit or stools (poo) from an infected person get into your mouth through: “• close contact with someone with norovirus who may breathe out small particles of the virus that you then inhale” We interpret that to mean that it is possible to breathe in norovirus...much as you might breathe in other viruses such as influenza or SARS-CoV-2. The only difference is that those are respiratory viruses, whereas norovirus is a viral infection that causes intestinal nastiness. How Can You Avoid Norovirus? There is no cure for norovirus. The only treatment is hydration. Some people become so dehydrated that they need intravenous fluids. That’s why prevention is the most effective strategy during an outbreak. That means being very careful about what you put in your mouth. Food or beverages that are touched by anyone who also handles money could easily be contaminated. That is why I have written extensively about coffee cups and dirty money at this link. It never fails to astonish me how many people push back about my cautions. Public restrooms pose a huge risk for infection. Knobs, door handles and almost any object in a public rest room should be treated as if it were nuclear waste. Hand sanitizer is not a substitute, unless it follows at least 20 to 30 seconds of scrubbing with soap and water. And if you walk into a public restroom where someone had either projectile vomiting or intense diarrhea, it is entirely possible that you will be exposed to the virus by just breathing the air. I know you hate the idea of masking...but you will hate the idea of vomiting even more! To prevent the spread of norovirus, conscientious hand washing is critical. Actually, that is an understatement! You cannot be too scrupulous in your hand hygiene! Air quality may also be a factor. How Easily Do Viruses Spread? Several years ago, researchers at the University of Arizona studied the spread of viruses by using a bacteriophage virus that resembles norovirus in size and shape (Sassi, American Journal of Infection Control, July 1, 2015). They put the test virus, which is noninfectious but easily detected, on a single door knob or table at the start of several research days in office buildings and a health care facility in Tucson. Throughout each day, they sampled other surfaces such as light switches, tap handles, bed rails or computer equipment. Nearly two-thirds of the surfaces studied had been contaminated within the first few hours of the day. The lead researcher, Chuck Gerba, PhD, determined that washing hands and using disinfectant wipes could stop this predictable spread almost completely. All we need to do is convince everyone to use these simple strategies. As your mother probably told you countless times, wash your hands. Don’t rely on hand sanitizer, as it does not work well against this virus. Scrubbing with soap and water works better. The Nay Sayers! Please take a look at some of the comments. These folks do not believe in the germ theory of disease. Noah thinks we should strengthen our immune systems through exposure: “I am wondering if, as a culture, we are overindulging in the use of ‘sanitary procedures’ such as constant washing of hands, massive use (abuse?) of ‘hand sanitizer’ and effectively minimizing the activation of our immune systems. “I presume that, much like our muscles, if our immune systems aren’t regularly challenged, tested gently, and required to be active they will not be as strong as they should be when we are faced with insult.” Try selling that message to someone in the middle of a norovirus attack. There is growing evidence to suggest that “viral reactivation” may contribute to dementia and other horrific chronic ailments. And no one wants to “strengthen” the immune system by catching poliovirus, tuberculosis or Lyme disease. Here is Julie’s comment: “I notice that the people who are most susceptible to bacteria-borne illnesses are the ones who constantly use hand sanitizers, Clorox wipes on surfaces, and are plainly in terror of everything not completely sterilized. “I wash my hands with soap (but usually less than 10 seconds) after using the restroom, don’t own a bottle of hand sanitizer, and invoke the 5-10 second rule if something edible (like a cookie) hits a floor, etc. “I’m rarely ill or suffer stomach viruses or other nasty maladies. I suspect it’s because I’ve developed a healthy immune system over the years by not being a germ-o-phobe.” And here is a response to the nay sayers from Jas: “I’M OUTRAGED! The reason why viruses, germs, fungi & bacteria thrive in the first place is that their hosts of transmission are ignorant, inconsiderate, lazy humans. Yes, viruses will still survive and get people sick... but how hard is it to wipe Purell on your hands? Really? It takes 10 seconds! (And what exactly are you going to do with those extra 10 seconds of not cleaning your hands? Save humanity???) “I got h-o-s-p-i-t-a-l-i-z-e-d with the norovirus, which I did track to the grocery cart I had used. God knows what baby poop or snot germs were on the cart handle, but it cost me, you and everyone else over $1,000 in insurance costs and lost wages for the ambulance, IV, over-night hospital stay, etc., just because you slobs out there don’t give a damn and think you’re invincible...? (Whiskey!-Tango!-Foxtrot!) “We live in our culture where people make more of an effort and spend billions of dollars to kill body odor, than kill the germs that can make them horribly sick or kill you! I say, label these stubborn, inconsiderate morons as F.O.Gs (Friends of Germs!) “I vote for the “Germ-a-phobes.” I’d rather live with reasonable preventative steps to protect my health and my family’s health than die with the plague... just because there’s a plague of idiots out there.” Don’t Forget to Disinfect: Washing up may not be enough, since flushing the toilet can spread infectious droplets around the bathroom. Consequently, the CDC recommends that bathroom surfaces be cleaned frequently with a bleach-based cleanser to disinfect them. “After someone vomits or has diarrhea, always thoroughly clean and disinfect the entire area immediately: - Put on rubber or disposable gloves and wipe the entire area with paper towels, then disinfect the area using a bleach-based household cleaner as directed on the product label. - Leave the bleach disinfectant on the affected area for at least five minutes, then clean the entire area again with soap and hot water. Finish by cleaning soiled laundry, taking out the trash, and washing your hands. “To disinfect, use a chlorine bleach solution with a concentration of 1,000 to 5,000 ppm (5 to 25 tablespoons of household bleach [5% to 8%] per gallon of water) or use an EPA-registered disinfecting product against norovirus.” Don’t want to measure 25 tablespoons of household bleach? The CDC offers this: “3⁄4 cup of bleach plus 1 gallon of water” Always wear disposable gloves and a face mask when cleaning up after someone who has experienced an intestinal apocalypse. Once you have cleaned up the mess and wiped everything down with a dilute bleach solution and left it for five minutes: “Step 4 Clean all surfaces again with hot water and soap Step 5 – Remove your gloves, throw them away, and take out the trash Step 6 – Wash all laundry that may have vomit or poop on it with hot water and soap Step 7 – Wash your hands with soap and water” A sick person should not cook for or care for others, as that might spread norovirus. There are tens of millions of people taking medications that suppress their immune systems. Many of them are advertised on television these days. A study in Clinical Chemistry, Jan. 3, 2025 reveals that people with less vigorous immune systems may shed viruses for longer than infectious disease experts realize. Food should be cooked completely, and laundry should be washed thoroughly with very hot water. Dry thoroughly at high temperature. We hope you do not catch nasty noro! If you have ever experienced this intestinal apocalypse, please describe it for the people who think “germs” are no big deal. You may want to let friends and family members know that norovirus is out there and spreading fast. We would be very grateful if you shared this article with them. If you were to also suggest signing up for our newsletter at this link, we would be even happier. Thank you for your support! Citations - Raglow, J. and Lauring, A.S., "Virus Evolution in Prolonged Infections of Immunocompromised Individuals," Clinical Chemistry, Jan. 3, 2025, doi: 10.1093/clinchem/hvae150

analysis.brief_en: A consumer-focused guidance article warns of a suspected surge in norovirus activity in the United States during 2025–2026, driven by a newly circulating strain (GII.17[P17]). Wastewater monitoring data show norovirus levels are currently 'high' and rising, with public health authorities noting substantial increases compared to prior years. The virus is described as highly contagious, with symptoms including sudden-onset severe vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, and abdominal pain. Transmission can occur via minimal exposure to contaminated surfaces, food, or vomit, and the pathogen remains infectious for extended periods even at freezing temperatures. While the CDC issued an early notice in January 2026, detailed surveillance data are pending, prompting the article to recommend heightened precautions.

Wastewater monitoring data show norovirus levels are currently 'high' and rising, with public health authorities noting substantial increases compared to prior years. The virus is described as highly contagious, with symptoms including sudden-onset severe vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, and abdominal pain. Transmission can occur via minimal exposure to contaminated surfaces, food, or vomit, and the pathogen remains infectious for extended periods even at freezing temperatures. While the CDC issued an early notice in January 2026, detailed surveillance data are pending, prompting the article to recommend heightened precautions.

news.content_title: 125 people sick in third Princess cruise norovirus outbreak this year
news.content: More than 120 people got sick in a norovirus outbreak aboard a Princess Cruises ship, marking the cruise line’s third this year. Among the 3,032 guests sailing on Ruby Princess, 102 reported being ill, along with 23 crew members, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Their main symptoms were diarrhea and vomiting. The health agency listed the impacted voyage dates as June 12 through July 2. The ship was sailing an Alaska and Canada voyage round-trip from San Francisco, according to CruiseMapper . More: Parasitic infection cases in Michigan explode in 10 days Princess said "a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness" during the trip. "Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, and cases have since decreased and remain low," the company told USA TODAY in an emailed statement. The cruise line also isolated sick passengers and employees, along with other steps, the CDC said. The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and "will be undergoing comprehensive cleaning and disinfection" before its next cruise, Princess added. The CDC has logged seven outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification so far in 2026. Two were due to E. coli, while the rest were caused by norovirus, including two on other Princess ships. There were 23 outbreaks that met that threshold in 2025, 18 of which were caused by norovirus, and the illness was behind 15 out of 18 outbreaks the prior year. While norovirus is frequently associated with cruise ships, those instances account for just 1% of all outbreaks reported . "(Outbreaks are) often taking place within the community, and oftentimes we don't know that they're happening," Sarah R. Michaels, an assistant professor at Tulane University’s Celia Scott Weatherhead School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, previously told USA TODAY. "Really, when we have these areas where people ... are in really close contact, things like day care facilities, nursing homes and cruise ships, it’s more likely (to be) diagnosed, reported and brought to our attention." This story has been updated to add new information. Nathan Diller is a consumer travel reporter for USA TODAY based in Nashville. You can reach him at ndiller@usatoday.com. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Princess cruise norovirus outbreak sickens hundreds of guests, crew

news.content: CruiseMapper Cruise news Accidents Third Norovirus outbreak on Lindblad's ship National Geographic... Third Norovirus outbreak on Lindblad's ship National Geographic Sea Bird in Alaska John Stansfield July 19, 2026 , Accidents The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported a third gastrointestinal illness outbreak aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird in less than 3 months. The latest incident occurred during the vessel's July 10th–15th, 2026 voyage in Alaska, when 18 of the ship's 62 passengers experienced symptoms including abdominal cramps and vomiting. The expedition vessel, operated by National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions , had previously recorded outbreaks during sailings from May 26th–31st and June 25th–30th . The first two incidents were confirmed as norovirus, while the cause of the most recent outbreak has not yet been identified, although the reported symptoms were consistent with the earlier cases. According to information provided to the CDC, the ship's crew implemented enhanced cleaning and disinfection procedures in accordance with the company's outbreak prevention and response plan. Additional measures included isolating affected passengers and crew, consulting with the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program and collecting samples to assist with the investigation. The CDC continues to monitor the situation remotely. Nat Geo Sea Bird operates seasonal expedition cruises along the coasts of Alaska and British Columbia during the summer months. The vessel accommodates up to 62 passengers in 31 cabins and specializes in small-ship nature-focused itineraries. For more National Geographic Sea Bird incidents and accidents, see the ship's CruiseMinus page accident virus Lindblad Expeditions National Geographic Sea Bird Alaska

news.content: Ruby Princess, a ship operated by Princess Cruises. — Wikimedia Commons - Z thomas At least 145 people were sickened in separate norovirus outbreaks aboard two cruise ships, federal health officials said. The outbreaks happened on the National Geographic Sea Bird and the Ruby Princess, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said. Both outbreaks were reported to the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program on Sunday, June 28. The main symptoms were vomiting and diarrhea. The CDC said norovirus caused the illnesses. On the Ruby Princess , 102 of 3,032 passengers reported being ill during the Princess Cruises trip, along with 23 of the 1,144 crew members. The Pacific Ocean voyage left San Francisco on Friday, June 12, traveled up to Alaska, and will end on Thursday, July 2, according to CruiseMapper . The Sea Bird saw illness reports from 19 out of 68 passengers, along with one of the 27 crew members. The Lindblad Expeditions voyage along the Alaskan coast started on Thursday, June 25, and ended on Tuesday, June 30. This was the second gastrointestinal illness outbreak on the Sea Bird in about a month. A dozen passengers and crew members became sick on a late May cruise, although the cause of that outbreak was unknown. National Geographic Sea Bird, a cruise ship operated by Lindblad Expeditions. — WIkimedia Commons - Dankarl Lindblad Expeditions, Princess Cruises, and the ships' crews increased cleaning procedures, isolated sick passengers and crew members, and consulted with the CDC. Princess Cruises also collected stool samples from sick people for testing. Cruise ships are required to report GI illness cases to the CDC. The agency defines acute gastroenteritis as three or more loose stools within 24 hours, or vomiting with another symptom such as abdominal cramps, diarrhea, fever, headaches, or muscle aches. The CDC has received seven outbreak reports from cruises so far in 2026

news.content: Health Alaska cruise struck by third suspected norovirus outbreak in weeks The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps By The News Digital Published July 17, 2026 A cruise ship sailing in Alaska has reported its third gastrointestinal illness outbreak in just two months, with 18 passengers becoming ill during its latest voyage, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The outbreak occurred aboard Lindblad Expeditions' National Geographic Sea Bird during a cruise between 10 and 15 July. Advertisement The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps. According to the agency, the cause of the latest outbreak is currently listed as unknown. However, the ship's previous two outbreaks, reported in May and June, were confirmed to be norovirus, a highly contagious virus that causes vomiting and diarrhoea. In response, the cruise operator isolated sick passengers and crew, collected stool samples for testing, consulted with the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program, and increased cleaning and disinfection procedures. The CDC said it is “remotely monitoring the situation,” including the cruise line's sanitation measures and outbreak response. The agency noted that cruise operators are required to report gastrointestinal illnesses quickly to help identify outbreaks and prevent further spread. It also said “norovirus is often a cause of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships,” although confirming the source of an outbreak can take time. Norovirus is commonly spread through contaminated food, water, surfaces or close contact with an infected person.
